tweet.text:
DeepSeek just open-sourced dsh-superagent-prototype, an agent that works your GitHub repos. Here's what you need to know.

It comes from the team behind DeepSeek Harness, the company's agent tool. It watches one GitHub repo, and optionally Feishu chats. When someone on an allowed list asks for something in an issue or PR, it opens a work item, takes a first pass, drafts a fix, and hands the result back for human review. The code is MIT licensed.

DeepSeek also published a design write-up, "Super Agent: Proactive Is All You Need?", by Yujia Qiao, an engineer on the harness. It first spread in China, and community translations into English followed within hours. The team says an official English version is coming soon.

The problem they describe is attention. People can only juggle about 3 to 5 agent sessions at once, so human attention becomes the ceiling. Their stated goal is to take as little human attention as possible and give as much value as possible.

The design has an always-on Router and many parallel Workers. Triggers include group-chat messages, emails, calendar reminders, GitHub comments and CI test results. The agent stays online 24/7 and picks up work on its own.

DeepSeek calls it research code, not a product. It grew out of the team's own day-to-day work on the harness.

Community reaction so far:
- Supporters see a possible "software factory" if it is set up well.
- Other builders say their own always-on agent systems landed on similar designs.
- Critics say the framing is about replacing slow humans with agents running many sessions at once.
- One prominent DeepSeek watcher claims that by late V4, DeepSeek's internal agent swarms reached the utility of Anthropic's Mythos Preview. They say it took swarms of 200 to 1000 agents, with a coordinator launching each next swarm from the last one's findings. They also claim the baseline is five swarms of 1000 agents per night. These are unconfirmed claims, not DeepSeek statements.

Key numbers:
- 3 to 5: agent sessions a person can manage at once
- 24/7: how long the agent stays online
- MIT: license of the prototype
- 200 to 1000: agents per swarm in the unconfirmed claims

The repo is deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype on GitHub, subtitled "Towards a More Autonomous Agent System".
